386: There is no accuser (about) a living one against Unas, there is no accuser (about) a dead one against Unas.
There is no accuser about a goose against Unas, there is no accuser about a bull against Unas.


387: If you do not ferry Unas, he will jump up and place himself on the wing of Thoth.
It is he (Thoth) who will (then) ferry him over to this other side.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber South Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
388: To say:
"Unas is he who has caused the land to be under water after he came out of the sea;
It is Unas who has plucked up the papyrus.
Unas is he who has appeased the Two Lands, Unas is he who has united the Two Lands, Unas is he who will unite himself with his mother, the Great Wild Cow.


389: Mother of Unas, you Wild Cow and wife, who (as a cow) is on the hill covered with grass, who (as a woman or vulture) is on the Mount of the Sehseh-bird!
They stand fast, the two Djed-pillars, the broken-off steps come down(?);


390: Unas ascends on that ladder which his father Re has made for him:
Horus and Seth seize the arm of Unas and take him to the Dawn Region.


391: He (Horus) to whom a wink was made:
"Beware of the one to whom (this) was ordered!".
He (Seth) to whom it was ordered:
"Beware of him to whom a wink was made!".
The face of the god opens for Unas, and this Unas sits down on the great seat at the side of the god.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber South Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
392: To say:
"O Height-Which-Has-Not-Yet-Been-Reached, Gate of Nun, Unas comes to you!
Let this be opened for him!
"Is Unas the little one there?"
"Unas is at the head of the followers of Re, Unas is not at the head of the gods who create trouble!"

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall Gable
pyramid_texts.t:
415: To say:
Unas comes to you, you hawks, although your houses are closed for Unas.
His loincloth is on his back, made of the hide of the a baboon.


416: Unas opens the gate with the double doors, Unas reaches the limit of the Horzon after Unas has put down there to the ground his robe with the tail.
Unas will become a Great One who resides in Crocodilopolis.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall Gable
pyramid_texts.t:
417 : To say:
Your deed be against you, what you will do will be against you, (O) Seksek-serpent, he who is in his hole (?), (O) adversary!"

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
418: To say:
Horus has fallen because of his eye,
the bull has rolled down because of his testicles.
Fall, roll down!

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
419: To say:
Babay has arisen, he opposes the god who rules Letopolis, who was protected by that spittle.
This (spittle)(also) protects everyone beloved by me.
You are loosed, O Wefy-snake. I cause Unas to be protected.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
420: To say:
O Unas! I have trampled the mud of the watercourses.
Thoth is the protector of Unas, when it is dark, when it is dark.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
421: To say:
Doer, doer, passer-by, passer-by,
(May your) face look backwards.
Beware of the great door!

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
422: Chastise Heku, Kebeb-he-heruby, O lion of Pehty, O lion of Pethety, the Pehty (and) Pethety.
Give me now, Heru-thubes, meat, now! One pot!
Go, go, serpent, serpent!

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
423: To say:
O this country, Mouth-of-the-River, this is the place of your overthrow.
This country, Mouth-of-the-River belongs to me, the Gold of Praise,
It is Haytau of Praise, this your Ox, the renowned one, against whom this has been done.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
424: To say:
Unas jerks indeed this his thumb, the left one, against you.
He gives a sign with it to Min, to the defenders.
O (you) who are used to rob, do not rob.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
425: To say:
The one bitten by Atum has filled the mouth of Unas while he twisted (himself) a twisting.
The centipede is struck by the inhabitant of the house.
The inhabitant of the house is struck by the centipede.
That lion (should be) inside this lion, the two bulls fight inside the ibis.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
426 : To say:
Your two drops of poison are on the way to the two poison vessels.
Spit out the two now, as they are overfilled with liquid.
O you who wink, you who are (adorned) with a diadem,
O Seshau, rain, that the snake may become fainthearted and the throat of my heart be saved!
Cloud, burst, that the lion be drowned in water and that the throat of the heart of the king be wide.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
427: To say:
O you who rush up as the young of the Water-pest, Themthy, Thenenu, Kebenu, those who glide away!
The Red Crowns praise the Tiu-shiy.
The Tiu-shiy belong to him who has elevated the Red Crowns.
Hail, we two!

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
428: To say:
He who makes his mother Neny,
He who makes his mother Neny,
Are you really in this, are you really in this?
Lion, be gone!

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
429: To say:
Heky-serpent, Hekeret-serpent, go away (with) face on the road.
Eye of Unas, do not look at him.
You will not do your will with Unas.
Get away, out!

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
430: To say:
The bull falls because of the Sedjeh-snake, the Sedjeh-snake falls because of the bull.
Fall, roll together!

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
431: To say:
A face falls on a face.
A speckled and black knife comes out against it.
It has swallowed that which it has seized.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
432: To say:
Your honor is effaced, O white hole, by him who has escaped the Feneth-worm.
Your honor is ravished from you, O white hole, by him who escaped the Feneth-worm.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
433: To say:
You (...) to the one who attacks, O Ikenhy-snake.
Your parentage (?) belongs to him whom you have attacked, O Ikenhy-snake.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
434: To say:
Back, invisible snake, make yourself invisible and do not let Unas see you.
Do not come in the place where Unas is, lest he pronounce against you this your name of Nemy, son of Nemyt.


435: A holy person falls into the Nile as a pelican.
Flee, flee
Brute, lie down!

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
436: To say:
Unas is Horus who comes out of the acacia, who comes out of the acacia, to whom it was ordered: "Beware of the lion (serpent)!".
He comes out to whom it was ordered: "Beware of the lion.".

437: Unas has come out of his djenyt-jar after he has passhas come out of his djenyt-jar after he had passed the night in his djenyt-jar.
Unas appears in the morning,
he has come out of his djenyt-jar after he has passed the night in his djenyt-jar.
Unas appears in the morning.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
438: To say:
The panther-cat springs on the neck of the serpent She-Who-Brought-Her-Gift (poison).
She repeats it (the attack) on the neck of the serpent Holy Head (or Uplifted Head).
Who is he who will be spared?
Unas is who will be spared.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
439: To say:
Thethu-snake (chainer?), whither?
You shall not go, stop for Unas!
Unas is Geb, Hemeth>-snake, brother of the Hemethet>-snake.
Shall the father die, the Damiu?

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
440: The hand of Unas is come upon you, the powerful one, the one which is come upon you.
(This hand is) the panther-cat (mAfd.t) which rules in the house of life.
She strikes you in your face, she scratches your eyes,


441: so that you fall down in your dung and glide down in your urine.
Fall, lie down, glide away, so that your mother Nut may see you!

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
442: To say:
Re appears, his Uraeus on his head, against this serpent which comes out of the ground, which is under the fingers of Unas.
He cuts off your head with this his knife which was in the hand of the panther cat, she who lives [in the house of life].

443: He draws those which are in your mouth (teeth), he saps your seed (poison) with those four strings which were in the service of the sandal of Osiris.
Monster, lie down! Bull, glide away!

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
444: To say:
The uraeus is for the sky, the centipede of Horus is for the earth.
One sandal (had) Horus when he stepped on the lord of the house, the bull of the hole, the fighting worm.
I will not be attacked (by him) (for) the sycamore of Unas is his sycamore, the refuge of Unas is his refuge.
(He) whom Unas meets on his way, he will eat him bit by bit.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
445: To say:
O Kherty of Nesat, ferryman of the Ikehet (barge) made by Khnum, bring this to Unas. Unas is Sokar of Rosetau. Unas is (on his way) to the place of Sokar, at the head of Pedju-she. Our brother of the two is he who brings these dunes of the desert.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
446: To say:
Your bread of eternity is yours, O Niu together with Nenet>, you two sources of the gods, who protect the gods in their shade.
Your bread of eternity is yours, O Amon together with Amonet, you two sources of the gods, who protect the gods in their shade.


447: Your bread of eternity is yours,
O Atum together with the Two Lions, who have created themselves, thier double divinity for themselves.
This is Shu and Tefnut, the two who made the gods, begat the gods, established the gods.


448: Say to your father that Unas has given you your bread of eternity, that he has satisfied you with what is due to you.
You should not hinder Unas when he crosses to him towards the Horizon.


449: Unas knows him, he knows his name:
Everlastingness is his name, Everlastingness, the Lord of the Year is his name, He with the arm ready to fight, Horus over the Milky Way of heaven, who makes Re alive every day.


450: He will build Unas again, he will make Unas alive every day.
Unas comes to you, Horus of Khat.
Unas comes to you, Horus of Shesmet,
Unas comes to you, Horus of the East.


451: Lo, Unas brings you your great left eye as healer.
Receive it from the hand of Unas, being uninjured, its water is in it uninjured, its red is in it uninjured, its breathing in it, uninjured.


452: Enter into it, take it into your possession, in this your name He-with-the-Divine-Ruler's-Decoration, that you may approach it in your name of Re.


453: Place it on your brow in this your name of Choice Oil that you may rejoice in it in this your name of Willow (Basket).


454: So that you shine forth thereby among the gods, in this your name of That-Which-Sparkles, that you may be pleased with it in this his name of Oil-of-Praise.
The Renenutet-snake shall love you.


455: Stay, Great Raft, as Opener-of-the-Ways, full of your spiritual power, coming out of the Horizon after having taken the White Crown in the great and mighty fountainheads in the south of Libya (as) Suchos, Lord of the Mountain of the Morning.
You travel towards your fields, you traverse your kesbet-groves, your nose inhales the perfumes of the Land of Shesemtet.
You let the Ka of Unas come near him like that your Wig which comes near you.


457: Purify for you Unas, make Unas bright in this your Jackal-lake, O jackal, in which you purify the gods.
You are powerful, you are sharp (as) Horus, the Lord of the Green Stone.
(to say) four times:
(like) the two green (fresh) hawks.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber North Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
458: To say:
The sky is serene (?), Sothis lives (i.e., shines), for it is Unas indeed who is the living (star), the son of Sothis.
The two Enneads have purified themselves for him as the Great Bear constellation which cannot perish.
The house of Unas which is in the sky will not perish, the throne of Unas which is on earth will not be destroyed.


459: Men hide themselves, the gods fly up, Sothis has let Unas fly towards Heaven amongst his brothers, the gods.
Nut, the Great, has uncovered her arms for Unas.


460: The two souls at the head of the souls of Heliopolis have bowed down at the beginning of the day, they who have passed the night while they made this bewailing for the god.
The throne of Unas is with you, O Re; he will not give it to any other god.


461: He ascends towards heaven to you, O Re, while his face (is like that of) hawks, his wings (are like those) of geese, his talons (like) the fangs of the god of the Djuf Nome.


462: There is no word against Unas on earth among men.
There is no crime of Unas in the sky among gods.
Unas has done away with the word against him, Unas has annulled it, in order to rise towards heaven.


463: The Open of the Ways has let Unas fly to heaven amongst his brothers, the gods.
Unas has moved his arms like a semen-goose, he has beaten with his wings like a kite.
He flies up, he who flies up, O men.
Unas (also) flies up away from you.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber North Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
464: To say:
You Gods of the West, you Gods of the East, you Gods of the South, you Gods of the North!
These four pure reed floats which you placed for Osiris when he ascnded towards heaven.


465: that he might cross towards the Cool (Region), while his son Horus was at his fingers (i.e., at his side) in order to let him grow up and let him appear as a great god in the Cool (Region), place them for Unas.


466: Are you Horus, son of Osiris?
Are you, O Unas, the god, the eldest one, the son of Hathor?
Are you the seed of Geb?


467: Osiris has ordered that Unas may appear as a second Horus.
These four spirits in Heliopolis have written it down in the register of the two great gods in the Cool (Region).

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber North Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
468: To say:
Hail to you, daughter of Anubis, she who stands at the windows of the sky, you friend of Thoth, she who stands at the two side rails of the ladder!
Open the way for Unas that he may pass.


469: Hail, O ostrich standing on the shore of the winding stream!
Open the way for Unas, that he may pass.


470: Hail to you, Bull of Re! You with the four horns,
Your (one) horn is in the West, your (one) horn is in the East, your (one) horn is in the South, your (one) horn is in the North!
Bow that Western horn of yours for Unas, that Unas may pass.


471: "Are you then a pure Westerner?
"I come from the Hawk-city!"
Hail, field of my peace!
Hail, [honored (dead) who are in you!
Unas will honor those] who are in you.
"Pleasant is the pure one who is in me."
(says the field).

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber North Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
472: To say:

The ladder is tied together by Re before Osiris.
The ladder is tied together by Horus before his father Osiris, when he goes to his spirit.
One of them is on this side, one of them is on that side, while Unas is between them.

473: "Are you then a god whose places are pure?"
"(I) come from a pure place."
"Stand (here) O Unas", says Horus.
"Sit (here) Unas", says Seth.
"Take this arm", says Re.


474: The spirit belongs to heaven, the body to the earth.
What men receive when buried is one thousand bread, one thousand beer from the offering table of He-Who-Presides-over-the-Westerners.


475: Is the heir grown poor, not having a script, (then) this Unas shall write with his big finger, he shall not write with his small finger.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber North Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
476: To say:
"How beautiful is indeed the sight, how good indeed to see." So say they, so say the gods, (when) this god ascends to heaven, (when) Unas ascends to heaven,


477: while his power is over him, the fear on both his sides; his magical power in front of his legs.
Geb acted towards him as it was done towards (himself).


478: They come towards him, the Divine Souls of Buto, the Divine Souls of Hierakonpolis, the gods of the sky, the gods of the earth.
They elevate Unas on their arms.


479: And you ascend, Unas, to heaven, (you) climb on it in this its name, Ladder.
"Heaven be given to Unas, earth be given to him." So said Atum.


480: He who spoke about it (to Atum) is Geb.
The abodes of my kingdom, the abodes of Horus, the abodes of Seth, the Fields of Rushes honor you in this your name Duau, like Seped he (who resides) under his kesbet-tree.


481: Has he killed you after his heart told him that you should die through him?
Lo, you come into being against him as the bull of the wild bulls who remained (after the fight).
He remains, he remains, the bull who remained (after the fight), and you will also remain, O Unas, at their head, at the head of the Spirits, for ever.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber North Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
482: To say:
A native of Heliopolis is in Unas, O God,
your native of Heliopolis is in Unas, O God.
A native of Heliopolis is in Unas, O Re.
Your native of Heliopolis like you is in Unas, O Re.
The mother of Unas is from Heliopolis.
The father of Unas is from Heliopolis.


483: Unas himself is from Heliopolis, born in Heliopolis when Re ruled the Two Enneads, when Nefertum ruled the human beings, (he is) one who has no second, the heir of his father Geb.


484: Any god who should stretch his arm (against him) - when the face of Unas is turned towards you in order to praise you and to call you on account of the person of Unas, O God, on account of his nose, O God - he shall have no bread, he shall have no cake amongst his brothers the gods,


485: he shall not send a sending, he shall not cover in his rut amongst his brothers, the gods.
The doors of the Night Barge shall not be opened for him, the doors of the Morning Barge shall not be opened for him.
His speech should not be judged as that of one in his city,
the doors of the Place of Annihilation should not be opened for him.


486: Unas comes to you.
Unas is a wild bull of the grassland, the bull with a large head, which comes from Heliopolis.
Unas comes to you, the wild bull of the grassland.
It is Unas from now on who gives birth to you, who continues to give birth to you.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber North Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
487: To say:
Hail to you, O Horus in the Horite sites,
hail to you, O Seth in the Sethan sites,
hail to you, Reed God in the Fields of Rushes,


488: Hail to you, you Two Harmonious Ones, daughters of the four gods who are at the head of the Great Castle, you who came out at the voice of Unas, naked!


489: Unas saw you, as Horus saw Isis,
Unas saw you, as Neheb-kau saw the Scorpion Goddess,
Unas saw you, as Sobek saw Neith,
Unas saw you, as Seth saw the Two Harmonious Ones.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber North Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
490: To say:
Unas is the thrasher of gods, who is behind the castle of Re, born from the goddess Wish-of-the-Gods, She-at-the-Prow-of-the-Barge-of-Re.
Unas sits before him,


491: he opens his chests, unseals his decrees, seals his book rolls,
Unas sends his messengers who do not tire.
Unas does that which he says to Unas.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber North Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
492: To say:
Should Unas be bewitched, Atum will be bewitched,
should Unas be opposed, Atum will be opposed,
should Unas be beaten, Atum will be beaten,
Should Unas be hindered on this way, Atum will be hindered.


493: Unas is Horus, Unas came after his father, Unas came after Osiris.
"O you, His-Face-in-Front-His-Face-Behind, bring this to Unas."
"What ferry shall I bring to you?"
"Bring to Unas the one which flies up, which alights."

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber North Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
495: To say:
See Unas, O Re, recognize Unas, O Re!
He is one of them who know you. He knows!
When his Lord comes out, he should not forget - the bon which (the king) gives - a prayer,


496: so that She-Who-Locks-Out-When-She-Locks-Out may open the doors of the Horizon for the coming out of the Morning Barge.
I know the Hall of the royal seat in the middle of the dias of the Zenith (?) from which though you come out


497: and descend into the Night Barge.
Order then, Unas - order him, order him - to speak the words four times one after the other, to these four raving ones who are behind you, who see with two faces, who speak in a roar(?)


498: which is evil for those who are to be (made) miserable, for those whom they want to annihilate.
(Give order) so that they do not put their arm (in the way of Unas) when Unas turns (his face) towards you, when Unas comes towards you,


499: (as) one who says to you your name of Great Flood, which came out of She-the-Great-One.
May Unas not be blind, when you place him in darkness.
May Unas not be deaf, so that he does not hear your voice.


500: May you take Unas with you, with you, him who drives away the storm for you, who dispels the clouds for you, who breaks up hail for you.
Unas will make you adorations (upon) adorations.
Unas will make you praises (upon) praises.
May you set Unas over the Vulture Goddess.

pyramid_texts.title: Antechamber North Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
501: To say:
May the bread fly up,
may the bread continue to fly up to my houses, to the houses of the Crown of Lower Egypt."

pyramid_texts.title: Corridor West Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
502: The phallus of Babay is pulled out, the doors of the sky are open.
The doors of the sky are locked, (the way leads) over the fire glow, under that which assembles the gods.

503: What lets every Horus glide through will also let Unas glide through, over the fire glow, under that which assembles the gods.
They make a way for Unas that Unas may pass along it.
Unas is a Horus.

pyramid_texts.title: Corridor West Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
504: To say:
"Back, you ox who should be slaughtered, in whose horns should be the fingers of Aker!
Fall, glide away!"

pyramid_texts.title: Corridor West Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
505: "Unas is a Ian-baboon, a Hetet-baboon, a Patet-baboon.
Unas' bottom is according to Unas' own wish(?), blessedness is on the head of Unas.
Unas will make the jubilations of those (i.e., as those) who jubilate.
He will sit among you, youthful ones."

pyramid_texts.title: Corridor West Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
506: "O Hemy and Sehed, Unas does not give you his magical power.
Unas will sit, his back towards She, the Holy One in Heliopolis.
Take Unas to the sky!"

pyramid_texts.title: Corridor West Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
507: To say:
"Unas came today, out of the overflow of the flood.
Unas is Sobek (the crocodile god), with green feather, with a watchful face, with uplifted brow, rushing up, coming from the leg and the tail of the Great One, she who resides in the brilliant light.

508: Unas came to his water currents, which are in the land of the flood of the Great Overflow (the sky), to the place of peace with green pastures, which is on the horizon.

509: Unas causes the grass to become green on the two banks of the horizon.
Unas brings the green brilliance to the Great Eye which resides among the pastures.
Unas takes his seat which is on the horizon.

510: Unas arises as Sobek, the son of Neith.
Unas eats with his mouth, Unas urinates, Unas copulates with his phallus.
Unas is the lord of seed, he who takes the women from their husbands, wherever Unas wants, according to the desire of his heart.

pyramid_texts.title: Corridor East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
511: [Unas is the Nau-snake, the leading bull] who has swallowed his seven Uraei, and so his seven neck vertebrae came into being, he who gives orders to his seven Enneads who hear the word of the king.

512: Unas has come, he swallows myrrh. Unas takes myrrh, he wallows in myrrh, the nails of Unas are (full of) myrrh.
Unas has taken your necks, O gods.
Serve Unas so that he invests you with your Kas.

pyramid_texts.title: Corridor East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
513: To say:
Unas is the bull of double brilliance in the midst of his Eye.
Safe is the mouth of Unas through the fiery breath,
the head of Unas through the horns of the Lord of the South.
Unas leads the god. Unas rules over the Ennead.
Unas lets the lapis lazuli grow,
Unas causes the southern tun to grow.

514: Unas has twisted the shem-shem-plant into ropes.
Unas has united the heavens.
Unas rules over the lands, the South and the North, (as) the god of those who were before.
Unas has built a divine city as it should be.
Unas is the third when he appears.

pyramid_texts.title: Corridor East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
515: To say:
Unas has regulated the night, Unas has sent the stars on their way.
The Powers appear, they honor Unas (with the title of) Babay.
Unas is the son of her who did not know that she gave birth to Unas, for Powerful Face, the Lord of Nights.

516: Humble (?) yourselves, you lords, hide yourselves, you subjects, before Unas.
Unas is Babay, the Lord of the Night,
The Bull of Apes, who lives without knowing it.

pyramid_texts.title: Corridor East Wall
pyramid_texts.t:
517: To say:
O you, Whose Back Is on His Back, bring to Unas the seferet of the offering-meal which is on the back of Osiris, so that Unas may ascend on it to heaven, so that Unas may serve Re as courtier in the sky.
